name: Baron Aquanis
summary: In the flooded Moonshrine Ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, Baron Aquanis rises from the depths when the Fathom Stone is disturbed. The Twilight's Hammer cultists occupy the ruins, and the Earthen Ring suspects the baron has been corrupted.

sections.title: Guardian of the Fathom Stone
sections.body: Beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins lies the Fathom Stone, surrounded by Twilight's Hammer cultists. A fathom core rests within it. Read properly, the device reveals the history of nearby elemental activity. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover it. Disturb the stone, and Baron Aquanis rises from the depths.

sections.title: Corruption of the Depths
sections.body: The Earthen Ring has long judged Baron Aquanis to be a corrupted elemental power. When he is destroyed, he leaves behind a Strange Water Globe. The impervious orb holds putrid, sloshing water that seems to have fed him energy. Je'neu Sancrea believes it may show what corrupted the baron and how. The Twilight's Hammer may be responsible, he says, though he wants proof.

faq.q: Where can I find Baron Aquanis?
faq.answer: Baron Aquanis dwells in the flooded Moonshrine Ruins deep inside Blackfathom Deeps. He rises when someone disturbs the underwater Fathom Stone, as Horde adventurers do while recovering its fathom core for Je'neu Sancrea.

faq.q: What is the Strange Water Globe?
aliases: what is the water globe for
faq.answer: The Strange Water Globe is left behind when Baron Aquanis is destroyed. The impervious orb holds putrid, sloshing water that seems to have fed his elemental energy. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring wants to study it for proof of what corrupted the baron and how.

faq.q: Why is the Earthen Ring interested in Baron Aquanis?
faq.answer: The Earthen Ring watches over the balance of the elements. Je'neu Sancrea and his comrades have long considered Baron Aquanis a corrupted elemental power. Since the Twilight's Hammer occupies the Moonshrine Ruins, they fear the cult may be coercing the elements against the Horde. The baron's remains and the fathom core could reveal what the cult is doing.

The fathom core is an elemental artifact housed within the sunken Fathom Stone. A trained shaman can read it to learn the history of regional elemental activity. It may also expose the Twilight's Hammer's dark rituals in the ruins.

faq.q: Is Baron Aquanis allied with the Twilight's Hammer?
faq.answer: As far as anyone can tell, Baron Aquanis is a corrupted elemental, not a willing servant. The Twilight's Hammer cultists in the Moonshrine Ruins are the obvious suspects. Je'neu Sancrea says their involvement would not surprise him, but he wants proof before he says for sure.

faq.q: Does the Alliance have business with Baron Aquanis?
faq.answer: Not directly. Je'neu Sancrea is an Earthen Ring shaman working with the Horde on Ashenvale's coast, and the Fathom Stone and Baron Aquanis are his concern. He sends Horde adventurers to recover the fathom core. Alliance explorers in Blackfathom Deeps have other errands there.

angles.text: For a shaman of the Earthen Ring, Baron Aquanis is a tragic example of elemental perversion. His tainted remains may offer insight into purifying twisted spirits.
Je'neu Sancrea works with the Horde on Ashenvale's coast. The fathom core his Horde helpers recover is meant to show what the Twilight's Hammer is doing to the elements there.
